title: Non-Homogeneous ODE
body:
[[Undetermined Coefficients]]

---

A linear ODE with something other than zero on the right:

$$
ay'' + by' + cy = f(t)
$$

$f$ is the **forcing term**: the external input driving the system, as opposed to
[[Homogeneous ODE|the homogeneous case]] where the system is left alone.

## The structure theorem

$$
y = y_c + y_p
$$

- $y_c$, the **complementary** solution, solves the homogeneous equation $ay''+by'+cy=0$ and
  carries all the arbitrary constants
- $y_p$, a **particular** solution, is any single function satisfying the full equation. It needs
  no constants and it does not matter which one you find

Why it works: if $y_1$ and $y_2$ both solve the full equation, their difference solves the
homogeneous one, by linearity. So every solution is one particular solution plus something
homogeneous, and there is nothing else out there.

**This is the same statement as $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$ in [[LINEAR ALGEBRA]]**: the solution set
is one particular solution plus the [[Kernel and Range|null space]]. Same theorem about a linear
operator, once with a matrix and once with $a\frac{d^2}{dt^2} + b\frac{d}{dt} + c$. The differential
operator is a [[Linear Transformation]], which is the whole reason any of this machinery applies.

## The order of work

1. Solve the homogeneous equation first, by its characteristic roots. That gives $y_c$
2. Find $y_p$ by [[Undetermined Coefficients]] (guess the shape of $f$) or variation of parameters
   (works always, more effort)
3. Add them
4. **Only now** apply initial conditions, to the sum

Step 4 is the one that goes wrong. Fitting the constants to $y_c$ before adding $y_p$ gives the
wrong answer every time, because the initial conditions constrain the total.

## Physically

$y_c$ is the **transient**: with damping its roots have negative real part, so it dies out. $y_p$ is
the **steady state**, the response that persists as long as the forcing does. Resonance is the case
where the forcing frequency matches a root of the characteristic polynomial, the guess collides
with $y_c$, and the repair (multiplying by $t$) produces a solution that grows without bound. The
algebraic special case and the physical catastrophe are the same event.
